newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares to consolidate until next week.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares to consolidate until next week.

text.p: Belgian shares fell on Wednesday and dealers saw no short-term respite until uncertainty over the strength of the U.S. economy was lifted.
"I think a bit more consolidation is likely. Then we should be able to go back up again, perhaps next week," said Paul De Lophem of brokerage Mignon, Hanart, Declerck.
"We are still in a consolidation phase. The parameters, such as the dollar, have not changed," said Bernard du Parc, head trader at BBL/Vermeulen-Raemdonck.
The Bel-20 leading share index ended down 0.92 percent at 2,031.67 points.

Dealers said the picture should become clearer next week, after publication of fourth quarter U.S. growth figures on Friday and the next meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy making Federal Open Market Committee on February 4.
Recent rising stars were among the hardest hit issues on Wednesday, with supermarket group Delhaize slipping 40 francs, or 2.07 percent, to 1,890 francs in active trade in 125,942 shares.
Only two Bel-20 issues bucked the trend. Oil group PetroFina rose 175 francs, or 1.54 percent, to 11,525 francs on news of a 38 percent rise in 1996 profit.
Utility holding company Tractebel rose 50 francs, or 0.34 percent, to 14,725 francs.

Dealers said Tractebel's rise was not however related to news after the close that its largest shareholder Societe Generale de Belgique was prepared to see private Flemish investors build up a stake in the company if they acquired their shares through the bourse.
Mignon's De Lophem noted Wednesday's volume in Tractebel was moderate and no big blocks changed hands.
